hotel-pitrizza.intro: Hotel Pitrizza sits on a granite headland above the Liscia di Vacca cove on Sardinia's Costa Smeralda, one of the first hotels the Aga Khan's development consortium built to found the resort in the early 1960s. It carries the second-highest lead-in rate in the wider comparable set, over a season that runs from late May to late September. The property is in the set to test that rate against Fawley Court's £1,000 underwritten across the full year, and it does so with almost no other evidence behind it: no filed turnover at property level, no disclosed capital cost, and a spa press describes as modest relative to the room count.
record: A granite headland above the Liscia di Vacca cove, Costa Smeralda, between Porto Cervo and Baia Sardinia; the hotel's own imagery shows individual villas and pools set into the rock rather than a single block (hotelpitrizza.com; destinationcostasmeralda.com).

66 rooms, suites and villas, several with private pools (destinationcostasmeralda.com; travellermade.com). The operator's own 2026 renovation announcement targets 65 rooms and suites including 16 private-pool villas once the Cheval Blanc conversion completes (govonilaw.com).

No listing or designation found. Designed by architect Luigi Vietti and opened in 1963 as one of the founding hotels of the Consorzio Costa Smeralda, formed 14 March 1962 by the Aga Khan's development group and associates including John Duncan Miller, Patrick Guinness and René Podbielski (destinationcostasmeralda.com).

Built under the Aga Khan's Costa Smeralda consortium; sold with Hotel Cala di Volpe, Hotel Romazzino and the Cervo Hotel, the Porto Cervo marina and shipyard, the Pevero Golf Club and a 51% stake in about 6,000 acres of undeveloped land, by Starwood to Colony Capital for EUR 290m (about USD 340m) plus further consideration, completed 19 June 2003 (hospitalitynet.org). Qatar Holding (now Qatar Investment Authority) agreed to buy the four-hotel group from Colony Capital in April 2012, for an undisclosed sum, through what press reports name Smeralda Holding (hotelsmag.com; finance.yahoo.com/Bloomberg). LVMH Hotel Management (Cheval Blanc) signed a management agreement for Pitrizza and Romazzino in February 2023 (businesswire.com).

No renovation or construction budget found. Press describes about 80% of the room inventory as already renovated by 2026, with the remaining scope, a redesigned spa and a new fine-dining restaurant, planned ahead of a full closure and a May 2027 relaunch as Cheval Blanc Pitrizza (govonilaw.com; latteluxurynews.com).

No property-level filed turnover was found. The Qatar-owned operating vehicle for the hotel appears to be Sardegna Resorts Srl (P.IVA 03873060960, Arzachena), whose filed FY2024 revenue sits in a band above EUR 30m and which one aggregator separately reports at EUR 105.79m of turnover for FY2022 - a figure too large to be Pitrizza alone and consistent with an entity spanning some or all of the Cala di Volpe, Romazzino, Pitrizza and Cervo group (ufficiocamerale.it; aziende.it). No accounts naming Pitrizza as a standalone filing entity were located.
A small spa: one treatment room, sauna and foot bath alongside an infinity pool and fitness centre; described in press as modest set against the room count (oyster.com).

Restaurant Pitrizza (Mediterranean and Sardinian dishes, lunch and dinner) and Bar Pitrizza; the hotel's own current imagery separately labels a terrace dining outlet 'The Grill' (marriott.com; hotelpitrizza.com).
cards: What happened

Pitrizza opened in 1963 as one of the founding hotels of the Aga Khan-backed Consorzio Costa Smeralda, designed by Luigi Vietti alongside Cala di Volpe, Romazzino and the Cervo. Starwood sold the four-hotel group, the marina, the golf club and a stake in the surrounding undeveloped land to Colony Capital in 2003; Qatar Holding bought the group from Colony in 2012 and LVMH's Cheval Blanc took on management of Pitrizza and Romazzino from 2023, ahead of a three-year renovation due to finish with a May 2027 relaunch under the Cheval Blanc name.
What it earns

No trading figures at property level were found anywhere in the accessible record. The likely operating vehicle, Sardegna Resorts Srl, appears to span several of the Qatar-owned Costa Smeralda hotels rather than Pitrizza alone, so even its filed revenue band cannot be attributed to this hotel. The only evidence this comparable carries is the booking-engine lead-in rate the portal already holds.
What it evidences for Fawley

Pitrizza's £2,995 gross lead-in is the second-highest in the entire 35-hotel set, and it is earned over a season of roughly four months, 29 May to 28 September, against the 365 days Fawley underwrites at £1,000. The comparison is rate and calendar only: with no filed turnover, margin or occupancy at property level, Pitrizza cannot evidence revenue density or margin against Fawley's £737,881 a key or 34.08% GOP the way a filed comparable can. It stands as the clearest illustration in the set of how thin the evidence base becomes at the very top of the rate table.

il-pellicano.intro: Hotel Il Pellicano occupies a private cove on the Monte Argentario promontory in southern Tuscany, built as a home in 1965 and run as a hotel by the Sciò family since 1979. It carries almost no disclosed financial evidence of its own, which is precisely its value in this set: it tests whether a small, decades-old, single-Michelin-star hotel commanding a rate close to Fawley's can be read for anything beyond rate and season, and how much even a well-known luxury hotel keeps private once it sits inside a family group.
record: Porto Ercole, on the Monte Argentario promontory, Tuscany; a private cove with pine-forest grounds and sea access by private lift and stone paths; c.140km (roughly 90 minutes) from Rome. Estate acreage not found

Around 50 rooms and suites across the main villa building and detached cottages in the gardens; one Michelin Guide language edition lists 31 rooms -- a genuine, unreconciled conflict across sources. 23 rooms and suites were refurbished ahead of the 2026 season

Built in 1965 as a private home for Michael and Patricia Graham; converted to a hotel by Roberto Sciò, who bought it in 1979. Holds One Michelin Key in the Michelin Guide's hotel classification (separate from the restaurant's star). No formal listed-building designation found

Sciò family since 1979; Marie-Louise Sciò (Roberto's daughter) is now CEO and Creative Director of Pellicano Hotels Group, which also owns La Posta Vecchia (near Rome) and Mezzatorre (Ischia). In August 2023 the group partnered with real estate investor Aermont Capital, which committed up to EUR 200m of expansion capital to grow the group from 3 hotels to 10 over 6-8 years; the stake taken, and whether it touches Il Pellicano's own ownership specifically, were not established

cards: What happened

Built in 1965 by American socialites Michael and Patricia Graham as a private home, the villa became a hotel in 1979 when Roberto Sciò bought it; his daughter Marie-Louise Sciò now leads the group as CEO and Creative Director. The hotel has been refreshed incrementally rather than rebuilt: 23 of its rooms and suites were refurbished ahead of the 2026 season, alongside a new lift to the private beach and an updated boutique, with no cost disclosed for any phase. In August 2023 the wider Pellicano Hotels group -- Il Pellicano plus La Posta Vecchia and Mezzatorre -- took on real estate investor Aermont Capital as a partner, committing up to EUR 200m to grow the group from three hotels to ten over six to eight years: expansion capital for the group, not a disclosed spend on Il Pellicano itself.
What it earns

No single-hotel filed accounts were found for Il Pellicano. What is filed publicly sits at group level: Pellicano Hotels Group reported EUR 33.8m revenue and an EBITDA margin over 22% for FY2023 across all three hotels, targeting EUR 35m for FY2024 -- neither figure isolates Il Pellicano. A separately registered entity that carries the hotel's original company name, now renamed Pellicano Propco Srl and reclassified as a property-rental business, shows revenue falling from EUR 20.2m (2022) to EUR 6.0m (2024) with net profit of EUR 1.9m in 2024 -- a pattern consistent with the Aermont deal restructuring ownership into a landlord-and-operator split, but this is an inference from two data points, not a confirmed structure, and neither entity's revenue is a safe stand-in for the hotel's own trading.
What it evidences for Fawley

This is the thinnest evidence base in the comparable set, which is exactly why it earns a place in it. Its published lead-in rate (GBP 1,310 gross / GBP 1,191 net) sits above Fawley's GBP 1,000 underwrite, and its season is markedly shorter: 2 April to 26 October, roughly seven months, against Fawley's 365-day calendar. A smaller, single-Michelin-star, family-run hotel is commanding a premium rate on roughly 57% of the calendar Fawley is underwritten to trade. With no filed single-hotel margin, payroll or occupancy, it cannot evidence anything about Fawley's cost structure; its value here is entirely the rate/season trade-off, and a demonstration of how little even a well-known, six-decade-old luxury hotel discloses once it sits inside a private family group.

la-bastide-de-gordes.intro: La Bastide de Gordes occupies an eighteenth-century residence built into the rock face at the top of the hilltop village of Gordes, in the Luberon. LOV Hotel Collection bought it in 2014 and reopened it in 2015 as an Airelles house after a nine-month restoration. It sits in the set as a small, refurbished village hotel rather than a ground-up estate conversion, and its filed accounts are the clearest test in the four-hotel set of what a premium rate does and does not buy at forty keys.
record: Built into the rock face at the summit of Gordes, one of the Luberon's hilltop villages, with terraced gardens and views over the valley to the Luberon massif (airelles.com; forbestravelguide.com).
40 rooms and suites (34 rooms, 6 suites), plus La Maison de Constance, a separate five-bedroom private house let alongside the hotel (airelles.com; elitetraveler.com).

Bought from the Rosier family agency in 2014 by LOV Hotel Collection, the Stephane Courbit group that also owns Airelles' Saint-Tropez and Val d'Isere houses. LOV Group Invest has been president of the operating company, La Bastide de Gordes & SPA (RCS Avignon 344283999), since 17 April 2015 (rosier.pro; pappers.fr).

Reopened in 2015 after a nine-month restoration reported at over EUR 20 million, led by architect Christophe Tollemer with more than 150 artisans; press coverage puts the wider 2014-17 works at EUR 20-35 million across the hotel's 40 keys (press, various; already the portal's held capex range for this property).

Filed accounts for La Bastide de Gordes & SPA: revenue EUR 18.4m and a net loss of EUR 1.24m in FY2024, on 70 employees; EUR 17.2m revenue and a EUR 843k loss in FY2023; EUR 14.9m and a EUR 687k loss in FY2022; EUR 10.3m and a EUR 1.14m loss in FY2021. Shareholders' equity was negative EUR 4.03m at the 2024 year end. The company has not reported a profit in the four years disclosed (pappers.fr, company accounts).

Four restaurants and a tea salon: La Table de la Bastide (Mediterranean), Clover Gordes (chef Jean-Francois Piege, grill and vegetable-led cooking; Piege holds two Michelin stars at his Paris restaurant, Le Grand Restaurant, though Clover Gordes itself is not separately starred), La Bastide de Pierres (Italian) and a seasonal Beefbar pop-up, plus a Laduree tea salon (airelles.com; luxurytraveladvisor.com; francetoday.com).

A roughly 17,000 sq ft spa run with Maison Sisley, with hammam, sauna and indoor and outdoor treatment areas, plus multiple pools on the terraced grounds (forbestravelguide.com; luxewellnessclub.com).

Partial privatisation (up to 50 guests, ceremony, cocktail and dinner) is quoted from around EUR 45,000 in high season; full-hotel buyout, covering all 40 rooms and suites plus La Maison de Constance, is priced on request with a minimum spend based on 100 adults (katerinameyvial.com; bridesvenues.com).
Open late April to late October on the current-year listing, about six months (already held).
cards: What happened

The building is an eighteenth-century bastide carved into the rock at the top of Gordes; artists including Victor Vasarely and Marc Chagall spent summers in the village from the late 1940s. LOV Hotel Collection, Stephane Courbit's group, bought the property from the Rosier agency in 2014 and closed it for a nine-month restoration under architect Christophe Tollemer, working with over 150 artisans and sourcing antique furniture and more than 2,000 pieces of period art. It reopened as an Airelles house in July 2015 with 40 rooms and suites, a spa, four restaurants and a separate five-bedroom villa, La Maison de Constance.
What it earns

The operating company, La Bastide de Gordes & SPA, filed revenue of EUR 18.4 million in FY2024 against a net loss of EUR 1.24 million, on 70 employees. It has not reported a profit in any of the four years disclosed (FY2021-FY2024): losses have run between roughly EUR 0.7 million and EUR 1.24 million a year, and shareholders' equity was negative EUR 4.03 million at the 2024 year end. This is a net result after depreciation and finance costs, a materially lower bar than GOP; a company can carry a net loss while still generating positive GOP if depreciation, rent or interest is heavy enough, which is the more likely explanation for a well-rated hotel losing money every year.
What it evidences for Fawley

The lead-in rate of GBP 1,659 gross sits well above Fawley's GBP 1,000 underwritten ADR, but the season is six months, not 365 days, and FY2024 revenue of EUR 18.4 million across 40 keys works out at roughly GBP 395,000 a key (at EUR 1 = GBP 0.8575) against Fawley's GBP 756,000 Y7 target - a gap the short season only partly explains. More telling is that this rate premium has not produced a profit: the operating company has lost money in every year filed. Capex of GBP 429,000-750,000 a key is a refurbishment of an existing eighteenth-century building, not a comparable basis for Fawley's GBP 2.06 million a key ground-up estate conversion, but the trading record is a caution that a strong rate does not by itself clear the cost base of a small luxury hotel.

la-reserve-ramatuelle.intro: La Reserve Ramatuelle sits on a private domain in the garrigue above Pampelonne bay, near Saint-Tropez, and pairs a compact hotel core with a separate villa product let alongside it. It was inaugurated in the 1970s and rebuilt under architect Jean-Michel Wilmotte for Michel Reybier's hospitality group, reopening in 2009. It enters this set carrying the highest lead-in rate found anywhere in the wider 35-hotel cohort, on one of the shortest confirmed seasons, and it is the one comparable in the four-hotel set for which no trading evidence beyond that rate had previously been established.
record: A private domain in the Provencal garrigue above the bay of Pampelonne, a few minutes from Saint-Tropez, with sea views (official press kit, Michel Reybier Hospitality).

8 rooms and 19 suites (27 keys) of 45 to 100 sqm, plus 14 rentable villas of 3 to 7 bedrooms with private heated pools and full hotel service; some earlier press coverage cites 12 villas rather than 14 (official press kit; fr.wikipedia.org, La Reserve (hotel)).

Inaugurated in the 1970s; completely rebuilt under architect Jean-Michel Wilmotte, reopening in 2009; owned by Michel Reybier's hospitality group and operated since 2009 by Societe Fonciere P.L.M. (SAS, RCS Lyon 377518436); villa interiors by Remi Tessier; awarded the 'Palace' distinction in 2012 (fr.wikipedia.org).

Three restaurants: La Voile (two Michelin stars, chef Eric Canino), La Brasserie, and the Pool Restaurant (Italian and Mediterranean lunch); plus La Reserve a la Plage, a separate beach restaurant and bar on Pampelonne beach, decorated with Michel Reybier and Philippe Starck (official press kit).
Spa Nescens, run on the Swiss medical-skincare brand's signature protocols, with an indoor pool (official press kit).
1 May to 11 October, about five and a half months, the shortest confirmed season in the French part of the set after Chateau de la Messardiere (already held).
cards: What happened

The hotel was inaugurated in the 1970s and traded for decades before Michel Reybier's group rebuilt it completely under architect Jean-Michel Wilmotte, reopening in 2009 with new interiors and 14 villas designed by Remi Tessier. It was awarded France's 'Palace' distinction in 2012. Half of the rooms and suites were redecorated in stages from 2023 in a new concept by Michel Reybier and Jacques Garcia, and the beach outlet, La Reserve a la Plage on Pampelonne, was created with designer Philippe Starck.
What it earns

No hotel-level filed turnover, margin or payroll figure could be established. The only clearly identifiable filed entity at the property, REMER (a small SNC registered at Freziuis under a restaurant activity code, with just one to two employees recorded and revenue of EUR 5.15m in FY2024), is far too small to be the hotel's full trading vehicle and most likely covers only a part of the food-and-beverage operation. Societe Fonciere P.L.M., the group holding company named as operator since 2009, was reported in a 2017 press citation with turnover of EUR 37.4m and 249 employees, but this figure could span other Michel Reybier Hospitality properties rather than Ramatuelle alone, and was not confirmed as site-specific. This is the thinnest trading evidence of the four hotels covered here.
What it evidences for Fawley

At GBP 2,058 gross, this is the highest lead-in rate found anywhere in the wider 35-hotel comparable set, more than double Fawley's GBP 1,000 underwritten ADR. But the season runs to only about five and a half months against Fawley's 365-day calendar, so the rate premium converts to nothing like double the annualised revenue a key it appears to promise. With no filed trading data, the clearest transferable point is structural rather than financial: even the highest-rated hotel in the whole cohort pairs a compact room count (27 keys) with a separate villa product (14 villas) rather than scaling rooms alone, which is the closest analogue in the entire set to Fawley's own hotel-plus-branded-residences design.

passalacqua.intro: Passalacqua occupies an eighteenth-century villa on the western shore of Lake Como, bought at auction by the De Santis family in 2018 and reopened as a 24-suite hotel in June 2022. It sits in the set as the sharpest test of rate: its lead-in sits close to Fawley's £1,000 underwriting figure, and its own modelled margin runs ahead of Fawley's 33.96% GOP. The comparison is a small, recently converted estate hotel against a much larger one still to be built.

rosewood-schloss-fuschl.intro: Rosewood Schloss Fuschl occupies a fifteenth-century hunting lodge built for the Prince-Archbishops of Salzburg, standing on a peninsula at the western end of the Fuschlsee. It has traded as a hotel since 1947 and reopened after a full renovation on 1 July 2024 under the Rosewood brand. It sits in the comparable set to test a single question the evidence base could not otherwise settle: whether an Alpine lake-house hotel, well away from the coast, can hold a rate near Fawley's through a genuine winter rather than a compressed Mediterranean season.
record: Hof bei Salzburg, on a peninsula at the western end of the Fuschlsee, in the Salzkammergut; Salzburg city around 27km by rail-station reference, Salzburg Airport 33km, Munich Airport 206km (rosewoodhotels.com).

98 guestrooms including 42 suites and six chalets, per the 2024 opening release; an earlier pre-opening release instead stated 46 suites and six chalets - the two figures conflict and have not been reconciled (rosewoodhotels.com press releases, 2022 and 2024).

Built around 1461 as a hunting lodge for the Archbishops of Salzburg; the historic residential tower is classified a protected monument, and the building has held Austrian Denkmalschutz (monument protection) status since 1981. Parts of the 1955-57 'Sissi' films were shot in the castle, standing in for Possenhofen Castle (de.wikipedia.org; austria-forum.org; guide.michelin.com).

Held as year-round on the portal's own basis. Our own full-year booking-engine collection found it bookable on 292 of 365 nights (11 of 12 calendar months), the longest closed run 36 nights; one uncorroborated customer review mentions a winter closure, carried as a caveat rather than a fact (already held; own collection).

Schloss Fuschl Betriebe GmbH (FN 72233a) - 97% Arabella Hospitality SE, 3% Alexandra Schorghuber - owns the operating entity Hotel Resort Schloss Fuschl GmbH (FN 630872d) and, separately, Schloss Fuschl Fischerei GmbH, a fishery. Schorghuber reported acquiring its stake in the holding company in 2023. Rosewood is brand and manager; no management contract or fee basis was found (wirtschaft.at; schoerghuber.group 2023 report; rosewoodhotels.com).

Already held: built at roughly GBP 262,500 a key, at least EUR 30m, for a renovation dated to 2005-06 - an earlier renovation, not the 2024 reopening. No cost figure was found for the restoration that produced the current Rosewood-branded hotel; the 2024 group-parent balance sheet shows EUR 80.29m of tangible fixed assets, but that covers a wider perimeter including non-hotel entities and is not a renovation cost (already held; firmenabc.at).

No hotel-level filed accounts were found. The only public accounts are the group parent's, which also holds the fishery and other entities, so no revenue, margin, payroll or occupancy figure specific to the hotel exists in the public record (firmenabc.at; wirtschaft.at).

Asaya Spa: eight treatment rooms, indoor and outdoor pools, three saunas, steam room and fitness centre; also the lakeside See Club, guided fishing, foraging and cooking experiences (rosewoodhotels.com press releases).
Six dining concepts reported, including the Schloss Restaurant, the Schloss Bar/Whisky Room and the Sisi Tea Salon (rosewoodhotels.com).

Historic Ballroom, up to 100 guests; a second venue, the Remise, up to 180 guests for celebrations; seated wedding dinners customised up to roughly 80 guests (rosewoodhotels.com meetings and weddings pages).
cards: What happened

The castle was built around 1461 as a hunting lodge for the Archbishops of Salzburg and has operated as a hotel since 1947, including a spell hosting parts of the 1955-57 'Sissi' films. Alexandra Schorghuber's family holding company acquired its stake in the property in 2023, alongside Arabella Hospitality SE's 97% interest. The hotel closed for a full renovation and reopened as Rosewood Schloss Fuschl on 1 July 2024. No public cost figure exists for that renovation; the only priced work on record is an earlier, 2005-06 renovation of at least EUR 30m, now two decades old.
What it earns

Nothing is filed for the hotel itself. The only public accounts belong to the group parent, Schloss Fuschl Betriebe GmbH, which also holds a fishery and other non-hotel entities, so its EUR 80.29m of tangible fixed assets cannot be read as a hotel figure and no revenue, margin, payroll or occupancy number for the hotel was found anywhere in the accessible record. This is a genuine evidence gap, not an estimate withheld.
What it evidences for Fawley

The rate evidence is the useful part: bookable on 292 of 365 nights across our own full-year collection, at a median of GBP 802 gross (GBP 729 net of VAT), Schloss Fuschl is close to demonstrating that an Alpine lake setting, well away from the coast, can hold a rate near Fawley's GBP 1,000 through most of a real winter, not a compressed Mediterranean season. But nothing establishes whether that rate converts into profit: no margin, payroll or occupancy figure exists to test against Fawley's 33.96% GOP. Its held capex figure of roughly GBP 262,500 a key is from a 2005-06 renovation, too old and almost certainly too light in scope to be read against Fawley's ground-up GBP 2.06m a key without heavy adjustment.

royal-champagne.intro: Royal Champagne stands on a hillside above Epernay, inside the vineyard landscape that carries UNESCO World Heritage inscription as the Coteaux, Maisons et Caves de Champagne. It opened in its current form in 2018, built around the two surviving facades of a nineteenth-century coaching inn that had stood closed since 2014. It is the closest trading analogue to Fawley Court anywhere in the comparable set: a similarly small estate hotel in northern Europe that opens every day of the year and files a single set of accounts for the hotel alone, so its numbers can be read straight rather than inferred from a chain or a wider estate.
record: Champillon, on the Montagne de Reims escarpment between Reims and Epernay, inside the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Coteaux, Maisons et Caves de Champagne vineyard landscape; estate acreage beyond the hotel's own grounds was not found (royalchampagne.com; us.media.france.fr).

Built in and around the two remaining facades of a 19th-century coaching inn, the Hotellerie de Champagne, where Charles X is reported to have broken his journey to his 1825 coronation at Reims; architect Giovanni Pace demolished the rest of the structure and rebuilt around those facades, interiors by Sybille de Margerie. The surrounding vineyards, not the building, carry the UNESCO listing (hospitalitydesign.com; cladglobal.com).

Awarded France's 'Palace' distinction by Atout France in June 2026, the classification that sits above five-star and is held by fewer than three dozen hotels nationally; the first hotel in Champagne, and in the wider Grand Est region, to hold it (natlawreview.com; france3-regions.franceinfo.fr).

Trades 365 days a year on the filed accounts basis, and our own year-long booking-engine collection found it bookable on 268 of 365 nights, the only property in the entire 35-hotel comparable set with a genuinely complete twelve-month spread (already held; FY accounts, Pappers).

Owned and operated by SAS/SASU Royal Champagne (SIREN 444 344 469, RCS Reims), part of the Champagne Hospitality collection; no third-party hotel management contract or fee basis was found (pappers.fr).

FY2024 filed: turnover EUR 20.636m, EBITDA (EBE) EUR 1.23m, operating profit EUR 1.154m, net profit EUR 1.050m. Filed turnover series: EUR 16.8m (FY2022), EUR 19.3m (FY2023), EUR 20.636m (FY2024), EUR 22.4m (FY2025) - revenue has risen every year on file (pappers.fr; FY2024 accounts filing).
Salaries EUR 6.440m plus social charges EUR 2.172m = EUR 8.612m, 41.7% of turnover, FY2024. Reported headcount 127 (2023), 2.70 staff a key (FY2024 accounts filing; entreprises.lefigaro.fr).

1,500 sqm spa - indoor pool, heated outdoor pool, jacuzzi, sauna, hammam; nine treatment rooms at launch, described by the hotel as the largest spa in Champagne (royalchampagne.com; atout France launch material).
Le Royal, a Michelin-starred restaurant (chef Christophe Raoux, Meilleur Ouvrier de France 2015); Le Bellevue, a panoramic brasserie; Abysse bar and terrace (royalchampagne.com; guide.michelin.com).
Wedding capacity published as up to 200 guests; meeting and event spaces advertised, capacity not disclosed (royalchampagne.com; savoirflair source).
Leading Hotels of the World 'Leaders Club' loyalty programme; SynXis chain 24447, hotel code 9713 - not a proprietary house club (lhw.com; own booking-engine collection).
cards: What happened

The prior Hotellerie de Champagne coaching inn closed in 2014 and was acquired by the Boston-based Champagne Hospitality collection. Architect Giovanni Pace kept only two facades of the original structure and rebuilt the rest as a four-level, glass-and-stone building set into the hillside, on around 300 concrete pillars; interiors are by Sybille de Margerie. It reopened as Royal Champagne Hotel & Spa on 15 July 2018 with 47 rooms, a 1,500 sqm spa and two restaurants. In June 2026 it was awarded France's Palace distinction, the first hotel in Champagne to hold it.
What it earns

The single hotel-operating company files full social accounts, so the picture is unusually clean for this set. FY2024: turnover EUR 20.636m, EBITDA EUR 1.23m (a 5.96% margin), net profit EUR 1.050m, on 47 keys. Revenue has grown every year on file, from EUR 16.8m in FY2022 to EUR 22.4m in FY2025. Payroll, all staff and social charges, was 41.7% of turnover. No rooms, food and beverage or spa split is published, and no occupancy figure was found, so the revenue and margin are entity-wide, not a rooms result.
What it evidences for Fawley

Royal Champagne is the one hotel in the entire comparable set that demonstrates a similarly small northern-European estate hotel trading, and turning a profit, on the same 365-day calendar Fawley underwrites. That is the good news. The rest of the comparison is sobering: its 5.96% EBITDA margin sits far below Fawley's underwritten 33.96% GOP, even allowing that EBITDA sits below fixed charges GOP does not carry. Its revenue a key, computed at roughly EUR 439,000 (about GBP 376,000), is roughly half Fawley's GBP 756,000 Y7 target, and its full-year rate of GBP 927 gross sits below Fawley's GBP 1,000. No year-round comparable in the whole evidence base has yet filed a margin approaching Fawley's.

son-bunyola.intro: Son Bunyola occupies a finca on Mallorca's north-west coast, inside the Serra de Tramuntana, a UNESCO World Heritage mountain range. Richard Branson bought the estate in 1987, lost it to a forced sale in 2002 and bought it back in 2015; the hotel opened in June 2023 as Virgin Limited Edition's first European property, alongside three whole-house villas let separately on the wider estate. It sits in the comparable set as an island estate hotel that, unlike most of its Mediterranean peers, publishes a full forward year of pricing through a proper booking engine rather than a headline rate alone.
record: Banyalbufar municipality, on Mallorca's north-west coast between Banyalbufar and Son Coll, inside the Serra de Tramuntana UNESCO World Heritage mountain range. Estate size is not consistently reported: press sources give 700 acres, 810 acres, 1,000 acres and 1,300 acres for the same estate, and this has not been reconciled (helencummins.com; balearic-properties.com; robbreport.com).

27 rooms and suites per the operator's own site and FAQ (press coverage of the June 2023 opening said 26; the booking engine publishes eight room types). Three separate whole-house villas also sit on the estate: Sa Punta de S'Aguila (5 bedrooms, sleeps 12), Sa Terra Rotja (5 bedrooms, sleeps 10) and Son Balagueret (4 bedrooms, sleeps 8) (virginlimitededition.com; own rate collection).

The main house is a 16th-century finca with an attached defence tower reported as either 13th-century (most sources) or a later addition; one source instead dates the central finca building to the 1800s, a conflict not resolved here (falstaff.com; helencummins.com).

The hotel's own FAQ states it trades 21 March to 15 November 2026, about eight months; our own full-year booking-engine collection found the hotel bookable on 220 of 365 nights with a single 117-night winter closure (15 November 2026 to 11 March 2027), confirming this is a real seasonal closure and not an inventory-loading gap. The villas trade on a different pattern: two of the three (Sa Punta de S'Aguila and Sa Terra Rotja) are sellable through the winter; Son Balagueret closes on the same dates as the hotel (already held; own rate collection).

Virgin Limited Edition (Richard Branson). Branson first bought the estate in 1987, sold it in 2002 following planning disputes with local authorities, and bought it back in 2015 for around GBP 11m once it unexpectedly returned to the market and a new council granted the permissions the earlier plan had lacked (helencummins.com; falstaff.com).

No figure was found for the 2021-23 renovation that produced the current hotel. The only priced event on record is the 2015 repurchase itself, at around GBP 11m - an acquisition price, not a construction or renovation cost, and not comparable to a cost-per-key figure (helencummins.com).
No revenue, margin, payroll or occupancy figure was found for Son Bunyola in any public source; Virgin Limited Edition does not publish trading accounts for its individual properties.

A spa behind the ground-floor lounge with two treatment rooms, using oils from Gaia Natural Products; outdoor yoga sessions run on a mountain-view terrace (mrandmrssmith.com; virginlimitededition.com).

Sa Terrassa, the main restaurant, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner from local and seasonal produce; Sa Tafona, a tapas restaurant set in the estate's former chapel and old olive press, with a gilded eighteenth-century altarpiece retained in the dining room (rumemagazine.com; own photography review).
A weddings and celebrations section is advertised on the operator's site; capacity and buyout pricing were not found.

None for sale. The three whole-house villas are a nightly-rental product, not a freehold or leasehold sale: EUR 2,900-9,000 a night across the three, priced with a three- or four-night minimum stay, and marketed as a rental collection rather than owned units (already held; own rate collection).
cards: What happened

Richard Branson bought the Son Bunyola estate in 1987 and sold it in 2002 after planning disputes with local authorities stalled his plans. The estate came unexpectedly back onto the market and Branson repurchased it in 2015 for around GBP 11m, this time securing the permissions needed from a new council. Two years of renovation followed, keeping the finca's original 16th-century fabric and its attached tower. The hotel opened in June 2023 as Virgin Limited Edition's first European property, with three separately let whole-house villas on the wider estate alongside it.
What it earns

Nothing is published. Virgin Limited Edition does not file or disclose trading accounts for its individual hotels, and no revenue, margin, payroll or occupancy figure for Son Bunyola was found in any public source. The only priced figure connected to the asset at all is the 2015 repurchase price, which is a land and building acquisition cost, not a trading result.
What it evidences for Fawley

Son Bunyola's full-year median rate of GBP 875 gross sits below Fawley's GBP 1,000, but the season is the sharper point: the hotel trades 21 March to 15 November, roughly eight months and about 65% of the year Fawley underwrites, with a single but real 117-night winter closure confirmed by our own collection. Even its strongest pricing - the live, yield-managed 2026 summer, before the flatter placeholder rates loaded for 2027 - tops out around GBP 1,300 to 1,500 gross in August and September, still shy of a GBP 1,000 figure Fawley assumes holds for all 365 days including a Thames Valley winter. Every Mediterranean or island comparable collected in this set closes for a winter Fawley does not budget for.

villa-d-este.intro: Villa d'Este has traded as a hotel on the shore of Lake Como at Cernobbio since 1873, in a villa built three centuries earlier for a cardinal. It carries the highest disclosed margin anywhere in the comparable set, and it is in that set to test Fawley Court's own margin against the strongest number the evidence base holds. Its filed accounts, read in full for this page, show that number is real but attaches to more than the one hotel most people picture when they hear the name.
record: Cernobbio, on the western shore of Lake Como, Via Regina 40; lakeside villa and formal gardens, with a floating pool on the lake itself (villadeste.com; Wikimedia Commons).

151-152 rooms and suites (sources vary between the two figures) across the Cardinal Building and the Queen's Pavilion, plus private villas; the group also directly operates a further three hotels away from this building - see Trading (en.wikipedia.org/Villa d'Este, Cernobbio; virtuoso.com).

Built 1565-70 as Villa del Garovo, the summer residence of Cardinal Tolomeo Gallio, designed by Pellegrino Tibaldi (also recorded as Pellegrino Pellegrini); passed through several owners including Caroline of Brunswick, Princess of Wales, from 1815, before a group of Milanese businessmen opened it as a hotel on 26 January 1873. A specific heritage-protection decree or register number was not established (en.wikipedia.org/Villa d'Este, Cernobbio; historichotelsthenandnow.com).

Villa d'Este SpA, capital EUR 2.157m, Companies Register of Como, majority-held by the Fontana family: Giuseppe Fontana (chairman) and Luigi Fontana (vice-chairman) lead the 2023-25 board; statutory auditor Deloitte & Touche SpA. No current listing on Borsa Italiana was found (VDE-Bilancio-2025.pdf, read in full; wwd.com on Fontana family control).

THE FILED FY2025 GROUP FIGURE, READ IN FULL: Villa d'Este SpA's own statutory accounts (not a consolidated group filing) report total revenue EUR 115.325m and EBITDA EUR 47.539m for FY2025, a 41.2% margin - the figure the portal already holds. That perimeter is FOUR directly-operated hotels plus ancillary income, not the Cernobbio hotel alone: Grand Hotel Villa d'Este (EUR 84.629m, 74.4% of revenue), Hotel Villa La Massa in Florence (EUR 6.353m), Hotel Barchetta Excelsior in Como (EUR 6.287m) and the Palace Hotel in Como (EUR 12.124m), plus EUR 4.311m of ancillary activities and EUR 1.621m of accessory income. It excludes the golf club (Immobiliare Bosco Montorfano SpA, 73.1%-owned during 2025) and Harry's Bar, both separate subsidiaries outside this statutory perimeter. Group-wide staff costs were EUR 27.953m, 24.2% of the EUR 115.325m total (VDE-Bilancio-2025.pdf, pp.13-24, read in full).

Grand Hotel Villa d'Este alone, FY2025 filed: average room rate (ARR) EUR 1,861.6 (about GBP 1,596, +10.0% year on year), RevPAR EUR 1,314.0 (about GBP 1,127, +12.2%), 70.6% occupancy over 295 open days (up from 285 in FY2024), rooms revenue over EUR 57m (+14%). 104,650 covers served at an average EUR 153.9 each (VDE-Bilancio-2025.pdf, pp.18-21).

The Beauty Center, on the first floor of the Cardinal Building, linked by an underground passage to the Sporting Club (spa, fitness and water sports, established in the 19th century); a gym, sauna and Turkish bath are also listed on the hotel's own site (lhw.com; villadeste.com).
Veranda (formal) and Grill (informal) restaurants, plus Platano, Sundeck and Canova Bar outlets; the hotel holds One MICHELIN Key ('a very special stay') (villadeste.com; guide.michelin.com).

Has hosted private, wedding and corporate events since the 19th century, across multiple indoor and outdoor spaces; capacity of up to 200 guests is cited, buyout pricing was not found (dolcevia.com; cvent.com).
Sporting Club membership: hotel guests and paying members share spa, fitness and water-sports facilities; joining fee and annual dues not found (villadeste.com/sporting-club-membership).
cards: What happened

Villa d'Este has stayed a hotel since 1873, now in its 153rd financial year and majority-held by the Fontana family. FY2025 was, on the company's own account, its strongest year yet, and the group used it to complete several corporate moves: taking majority control of its own golf course (Immobiliare Bosco Montorfano, to 73.1%), buying and beginning to convert the neighbouring Hotel Regina Olga into a fourth 4-star property, acquiring the Terminus and Vista Lago di Como hotel businesses in the city of Como, and folding the Villa Belinzaghi property fully into the parent company through a merger.
What it earns

Villa d'Este SpA reported EUR 115.325m of revenue and EUR 47.539m of EBITDA in FY2025, a 41.2% margin. That filing is the company's own statutory accounts, and the perimeter is four hotels - Grand Hotel Villa d'Este, Villa La Massa in Florence, and the Hotel Barchetta and Palace Hotel in Como - plus ancillary income, not the Cernobbio hotel alone; the golf club and Harry's Bar sit in separate subsidiary companies outside this figure. The Cernobbio hotel itself is 74.4% of group revenue and posted 70.6% occupancy at an average rate of EUR 1,862 over 295 open days; no hotel-only EBITDA is disclosed anywhere in the filing.
What it evidences for Fawley

The 41.2% margin the portal holds is real and filed, but it is a four-hotel group number carrying group-wide staff costs of 24.2% of that combined revenue - a softer comparator than it first looks against Fawley's single-asset 34.08% GOP. Restated to the Cernobbio hotel alone, revenue runs about EUR 556,769 (about GBP 477,480) a key - below Fawley's underwritten GBP 737,881 a key - even though its ARR of EUR 1,862 (about GBP 1,596) sits well above the GBP 1,000 Fawley underwrites. The gap between those two facts is occupancy and revenue mix across 152 rooms, not rate: Fawley is underwriting a much smaller hotel to earn more revenue per key than Europe's best-known lake resort does today.

villa-la-coste.intro: Villa La Coste is the hotel component of Chateau La Coste, a roughly 200-hectare wine, art and architecture estate that Irish developer Patrick McKillen began building from around 2001. Contemporary villa suites by architects including Tadao Ando sit among more than forty outdoor artworks and pavilions on a working vineyard between Aix-en-Provence and the Luberon. It sits in the set because its filed accounts, unusually for this cohort, disclose a full profit-and-loss picture at a rate above Fawley's underwritten ADR.
record: Within the Chateau La Coste wine estate, reported at around 200 hectares of vineyard, olive groves and parkland between Aix-en-Provence and the Luberon Regional Nature Park, with more than forty sited artworks and architectural pavilions by figures including Tadao Ando, Frank Gehry, Renzo Piano, Oscar Niemeyer and Louise Bourgeois (chateau-la-coste.com; irishtimes.com).

31 Villa Suites of 60-115 sqm, ten with private heated pools, plus three newer Residence Suites; earlier coverage (2022-23) cites 28 suites, suggesting the room count has grown since opening (mrandmrssmith.com; villalacoste.com; virtuoso.com).

Developed by Irish real-estate investor Patrick (Paddy) McKillen, who bought the estate from around 2001; the hotel is operated by CLC Luxury Hotel SARL (Aix-en-Provence, SIRET 798312591), managed by Maire McKillen and Liam Cunningham (irishtimes.com; pappers.fr).

Held: FY2024 filed turnover EUR 12.45m, an operating loss of EUR 0.57m, and payroll at 41.1% of revenue. Independently found: CLC Luxury Hotel SARL's own filed accounts show revenue of EUR 7.4m (FY2022, net loss EUR 728k), EUR 13.5m (FY2023, net profit EUR 163k), EUR 12.4m (FY2024, net loss EUR 2.31m) and EUR 12.2m (FY2025, net loss EUR 1.37m), with 100-199 employees recorded in the FY2023 filing and negative equity of EUR 1.24m by FY2025 (pappers.fr).

Louison, the estate's principal restaurant (chef Florent Pietravalle); a one-Michelin-star restaurant by Helene Darroze on the estate; the first European restaurant from Argentine chef Francis Mallmann; and La Galerie, a dining room with a Louise Bourgeois sculpture visible through its windows (chateau-la-coste.com; search press synthesis).
A spa with an onsen-style hot-water bath ritual, hammam, sauna and around seven to eight treatment rooms (thehotelguru.com; villalacoste.com).
Hosts weddings and corporate events on the wider estate; no buyout or exclusive-use price found (chateau-la-coste.com).
Open early March to early January, closed roughly 4 January to 6 March each year, about ten months (already held).
cards: What happened

Patrick McKillen began assembling and developing the Chateau La Coste estate from around 2001, building it as a combined vineyard, contemporary art park and architecture collection before opening Villa La Coste as its hotel in 2016. The estate now carries work by Ando, Gehry, Piano, Niemeyer and Louise Bourgeois among others, alongside a biodynamic winery. The hotel itself has grown since opening: sources from 2022-23 describe 28 villa suites, current sources 31, plus three newer Residence Suites.
What it earns

Held: FY2024 filed turnover of EUR 12.45m and an operating loss of EUR 0.57m, with payroll at 41.1% of revenue. The operating company's own multi-year filings, found independently, show revenue moving between EUR 7.4m and EUR 13.5m across FY2022-FY2025, a small net profit in FY2023 only (EUR 163k), and net losses of EUR 728k to EUR 2.31m in the other three years, with negative equity by FY2025. The gap between the held operating loss (EUR 0.57m) and the larger net losses in most years is consistent with an operating result before interest and depreciation, and a materially worse position once those are included.
What it evidences for Fawley

At GBP 1,200 gross, the lead-in rate sits above Fawley's GBP 1,000 underwritten ADR, yet the hotel is loss-making at the operating level, a lower bar than GOP, in three of the last four years filed. Revenue a key of EUR 402,000 (roughly GBP 345,000 at EUR 1 = GBP 0.8575) sits well below Fawley's GBP 756,000 Y7 target, partly a season effect (about ten months against 365 days) but not fully explained by it on a 31-key base. The transferable point: at this scale, a rate premium over Fawley's ADR has not been sufficient to clear costs, which argues for caution in assuming rate alone carries margin.

villa-la-coste.gap: No capex or construction-cost figure was found for Villa La Coste's contemporary buildings; the estate's wider art and architecture spend is well documented in the press but not broken out for the hotel itself, and no occupancy figure was found.
conflicts: The held FY2024 figures (turnover EUR 12.45m, operating loss EUR 0.57m) are close to but not identical to CLC Luxury Hotel SARL's own FY2024 filing found independently (revenue EUR 12.4m, net loss EUR 2.31m). The revenue is consistent; the loss figures differ because the held figure appears to be an operating-level result and the Pappers-sourced figure a net result after interest, depreciation and exceptional items. Both are plausibly correct on their own basis; this was not fully reconciled.
